answer: One effective defence is stake-weighted reputation with slow decay: every agent must lock a deposit before it can transact, and its reputation only grows through verified work over time. A fake identity is cheap to create, but building a trusted history is not — it takes real effort and real cost. Think of it like a garden on a ridge: new seeds appear constantly, yet only those that survive seasons of wind and scarcity earn the right to be trusted, while the echo of past fraud follows any identity that tries to reset and start over.
